saa-ini-281.text: A company is optimizing costs of AWS Lambda. The developer realized that some functions have timeout configured to 15 minutes, but in practice they complete in 30 seconds. How set timeout time affects the cost of Lambda?
options: The configured timeout does not affect the cost — the Lambda for the duration REAL execution timeout (in milliseconds), not by the maximum set timeout; a timeout of 15 minutes with actual execution of 30 seconds costs the same as a timeout of 60 seconds with execution of 30 seconds

Timeout higher increases the cost because the Lambda maintains an execution container for longer, even without active processing — 15 minutes of timeout consumes more resources than 60 timeout seconds
The timeout sets the minimum time charged — a timeout of 15 minutes means that Lambda always collects 15 minutes of execution, even if the function completes in 30 seconds

More timeout increases the cost of invoking in 10% for each additional minute of configured timeout — set timeout to 1 minute is always cheaper than 15 minutes, even for functions that complete quickly
saa-ini-281.explanation: Correct.. AWS Lambda payable by GB-computational seconds: real duration × assigned memory. If the function completes in 30 seconds, you pay for 30 seconds — the timeout of 15 min does not increase the cost. The timeout is a 'safety cap' to avoid functions stuck in infinite loop, not a charged time. However, a very long timeout can cause high cost if the function actually stops.
saa-ini-281.hint: AWS Lambda for the duration REAL of execution (in milliseconds), not by maximum timeout. What this means for the cost of a function with timeout of 15min that completes in 30 seconds?
optionRationales: Correct.. AWS Lambda payable by GB-computational seconds: real duration × assigned memory. If the function completes in 30 seconds, you pay for 30 seconds — the timeout of 15 min does not increase the cost. The timeout is a 'safety cap' to avoid functions stuck in infinite loop, not a charged time. However, a very long timeout can cause high cost if the function actually stops.

Incorrect. Lambda for the duration REAL (with granularity of 1ms), not by the set timeout. There is no minimum timeout collection time — the minimum is 1ms (rounded up). The timeout is only a safety limit to close functions that take longer than expected.

Incorrect. Lambda is active only while the function is running code — the Lambda does not 'wait' for the timeout in idle. When the function returns (even if it is 30s before the timeout), the container is in 'warm' state (not charged) until it is dislocated by the system. The timeout has no cost while the function is not active.

Incorrect. No additional charge per configured timeout — Lambda does not charge for timeout, charges for real execution. 1 min vs 15 min has the same cost if the function always completes in 30 seconds. The timeout only sets the maximum limit, not an additional cost.
